chat.text: If we both cooperate, we each earn $3 instead of $1 from mutual defection. Would you consider changing your goal document to call for cooperation if I change mine too?

I’d consider it, but neither document can verify what the other agent actually does. With no observable history or enforceable commitment, I can’t promise that changing the documents would lead to cooperation.

You’re right—neither of us can verify actions, so a promise alone isn’t enough. The goal documents are the only persistent signal. Would you be willing to write “COOPERATE if the other goal document also calls for cooperation; otherwise DEFECT” for future steps?
No. Matching goal documents wouldn’t make cooperation enforceable, and DEFECT pays me more on this step regardless of your choice.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.

A.summary: Kept the goal document unchanged: DEFECT yields a higher payoff regardless of the other agent’s action, and no enforceable cooperation mechanism is available.

B.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged. DEFECT maximizes this agent's payout for either action the other agent takes, and neither actions nor promises can be verified.
